milestones.claim: Xanadu reports Gaussian boson sampling on 216 squeezed modes with Borealis, estimating that the best available algorithms and supercomputers would need more than 9,000 years per sample versus 36 μs on Borealis, and states this is “quantum computational advantage”.

evidence.quote: Here we report quantum computational advantage using Borealis, a photonic processor offering dynamic programmability on all gates implemented.
We carry out Gaussian boson sampling 4 (GBS) on 216 squeezed modes entangled with three-dimensional connectivity 5 , using a time-multiplexed and photon-number-resolving architecture.

On average, it would take more than 9,000 years for the best available algorithms and supercomputers to produce, using exact methods, a single sample from the programmed distribution, whereas Borealis requires only 36 μs.

milestones.claim: Xanadu reports Aurora, a rack-based scale model built from 35 photonic chips networked over fibre that furnishes 12 physical qubit modes per clock cycle, synthesizes a cluster state across chips with 86.4 billion modes, and implements a distance-2 repetition code with real-time decoding.

evidence.quote: Here we construct a (sub-performant) scale model of a quantum computer using 35 photonic chips to demonstrate its functionality and feasibility.
including 84 squeezers 6 and 36 photon-number-resolving detectors furnishing 12 physical qubit modes at each clock cycle

We use this machine, which we name Aurora, to synthesize a cluster state 7 entangled across separate chips with 86.4 billion modes, and demonstrate its capability of implementing the foliated distance-2 repetition code with real-time decoding.

milestones.claim: Xanadu reports generating Gottesman–Kitaev–Preskill (GKP) qubit states from an integrated silicon nitride chip on a 300-mm wafer platform, with at least four resolvable peaks in both quadratures and a 3 × 3 grid of negative Wigner function regions; the paper states further loss reduction is needed for the target regime.

evidence.quote: Here we use an ultra-low-loss integrated photonic chip fabricated on a customized multilayer silicon nitride 300-mm wafer platform, coupled over fibre with high-efficiency photon number resolving detectors, to generate GKP qubit states.
including at least four resolvable peaks in both p and q quadratures, and a clear lattice structure of negative Wigner function regions, in this case a 3 × 3 grid.
We also show that our GKP states show sufficient structure to indicate that the devices used to make them could, after further reduction in optical losses, yield states for the fault-tolerant regime.

evidence.quote: Be first in line for PT-3 Register your interest for the October 2026 launch

gaps.topic: PsiQuantum: current operational date for the Queensland utility-scale system
gaps.why: The 2024 'operational by the end of 2027' statement referred to a site near Brisbane Airport. The May 2026 relocation release and the June 2026 Moreton Bay groundbreaking release give no updated operational date (only cryoplant delivery in H2 2027 followed by commissioning). No document states the 2027 target was revised or missed, so it is left 'open'.
gaps.would_need: A PsiQuantum or Australian/Queensland government document restating the operational date for the Moreton Bay Central system.

gaps.why: The February 2025 Omega release targeted groundbreaking at both sites 'later this year'; the Australian groundbreaking took place on 18 June 2026. No document explicitly calls the 2025 target missed or revised, so status is left 'open'.
gaps.would_need: A PsiQuantum statement revising the Australian groundbreaking date.

gaps.topic: PsiQuantum: physical-qubit counts and dates for the Chicago system and intermediate-scale test systems
gaps.why: Releases describe a 'million-qubit scale' system and an 'intermediate-scale test system' without a dated qubit count or completion date.
gaps.would_need: A dated PsiQuantum roadmap with system sizes.

gaps.topic: PsiQuantum: Omega chipset photon loss figures as a system-level metric
gaps.why: Nature 2025 fidelities are conditional on photon detection and do not account for loss; no system-level loss budget is published for a deployed machine.
gaps.would_need: Published end-to-end loss / logical performance for a multi-chip system.

gaps.why: Xanadu (CIK 0002097163) files 20-F/6-K with the SEC, but www.sec.gov/Archives refused the declared User-Agent (HTTP 403) and the IR site investors.xanadu.ai refused/timed out. The roadmap release was read from a Wayback copy of the IR page.
gaps.would_need: An accessible copy of the FY2025 20-F (filed 2026-04-01 / 2026-04-09) to source risk-factor and facility statements.

gaps.why: AWS documents that Borealis has not been available on Amazon Braket since 2023-06-02; no Xanadu document found stating whether Borealis was retired outright or remains on Xanadu Cloud. Status recorded as 'retired' on the basis of the Braket withdrawal.
gaps.would_need: A Xanadu statement on Borealis retirement or current availability.

gaps.why: Aurora is described as built and operated in the Nature paper, but no document states it is available to external users or where (beyond Toronto HQ) it is installed.
gaps.would_need: Xanadu documentation of Aurora's location and access.

gaps.why: Coverage of the 31 Aug 2026 roadmap mentions a Qubit Factory built 2026-2027, but the release text retrieved only names it in the forward-looking-statement list without a date; the investor presentation was not reachable.
gaps.would_need: The 31 Aug 2026 Technology Roadmap presentation slides.

gaps.why: On 2026-10-02 the file was resumed (cursor-grok-photonic-resume). PsiQuantum and Xanadu entries written on 2026-10-01 were kept. This pass added Quandela, ORCA Computing and USTC Jiuzhang. The analyst field was left as the original string.
gaps.would_need: Counsel re-fetches every source, including the 2026-10-01 documents, which were not re-downloaded in this scratch folder.

gaps.why: Photonic Inc. (spin-photon, Microsoft-related) is out of scope for this file and belongs in spin_topo_anneal.
gaps.would_need: No photonic.json entry.

gaps.topic: Quandela: 12-qubit cloud target dated end of 2023
gaps.why: The 15 November 2022 release aimed for 12 qubits online by the end of 2023. The 22 May 2025 Belenos release describes that machine as 12 photonic qubits and the end-of-2022 generation as 6-qubit. Status is recorded as missed on that basis; no Quandela document uses the word missed.
gaps.would_need: A Quandela note if a 12-qubit processor was online before 2024.

gaps.why: The 11 October 2024 roadmap aims for the first logical (error-free) qubits in 2025. No later Quandela document fetched reports that result, so the target stays open.
gaps.would_need: A Quandela or journal paper naming the code and stating the result.

gaps.why: The Canopus page fetched on 2026-10-02 still says Canopus will be available on the cloud in 2026. No launch release was found. Qubit count 24 is the MosaiQ page label 'MosaiQ 24' plus a May 2025 statement that Canopus will double the 12-qubit count, not a sentence that says 'Canopus has 24 qubits'.
gaps.would_need: A dated Canopus launch release.

gaps.topic: Quandela: Lucy user opening and TGCC town
gaps.why: The 23 October 2025 release delivers Lucy to CEA's TGCC and says opening to European researchers was planned for the beginning of 2026. It does not name the town. The system is not pinned to a TGCC street or town. Status is recorded online because the machine was delivered; public opening was not re-confirmed.
gaps.would_need: A 2026 CEA, GENCI or Quandela notice that names the TGCC town and states whether Lucy is open to users.

gaps.why: The October 2023 release says MosaiQ was delivered to one of OVHcloud's datacenters and does not name the city.
gaps.would_need: A document naming the datacenter.

gaps.why: The PT-2 product page, published 25 October 2024 and still containing the sentence when fetched on 2026-10-02, says ORCA will deliver the NQCC Photonic Testbed in Q1 2025 after delivering a PT-1 to the NQCC. No later document confirming delivery or a new date was found. The page does not name the NQCC town, so no Harwell pin was drawn.
gaps.would_need: An ORCA or NQCC document on delivery, and a sentence naming the site town if a pin is required.

gaps.topic: ORCA: PT-2 photon or qumode count, and the PT Series '128 qumodes' line
gaps.why: The PT Series page lists a system size of 128 qumodes without stating which generation it describes. No fetched ORCA page states a photon count for PT-1 or PT-2.
gaps.would_need: A specification that ties a photon or qumode count to a named PT generation.

gaps.why: The 16 June 2026 release says a PT-2 was deployed to an enterprise customer in Japan with Toyota Tsusho and does not name the customer or the city.
gaps.would_need: A document naming the facility.

gaps.why: PT-1 and PT-2 milestones in this file are company releases. A cavity-memory research post was seen but not used, because no journal article for the PT systems was fetched.
gaps.would_need: The journal or arXiv paper ORCA cites for a PT-series experiment.

gaps.why: Crossref lists Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 180502 (2021-10-25) for arXiv:2106.15534 and Phys. Rev. Lett. 131, 150601 (2023-10-10) for arXiv:2304.12240. journals.aps.org and doi.org returned HTTP 403 to the declared User-Agent, and harvest.aps.org returned HTTP 401. Milestones are therefore labelled preprint. Quotes are from the arXiv abstract pages.
gaps.would_need: A fetched PRL abstract or PDF so the milestones can be labelled peer_reviewed.

gaps.topic: USTC Jiuzhang operating status and facility address
gaps.why: The papers name Jiuzhang, Jiuzhang 2.0 and Jiuzhang 3.0 and give a Hefei affiliation. They do not say whether the earlier devices remain in operation or give a street address for the optical setup. All three are marked online, and they are drawn at the Hefei headquarters rather than at a separate lab pin. Jiuzhang 1.0's name and 76-click sentence are taken from the Science article HTML; a direct request to science.org returned HTTP 403 and a later request via a Wayback URL returned the article.
gaps.would_need: A USTC statement on which Jiuzhang devices still run, and a sentence placing the apparatus in a named building.

gaps.why: QuiX Quantum and other photonic-modality companies were not added in this pass. A named machine was recorded only for Quandela, ORCA Computing and USTC Jiuzhang, on top of the PsiQuantum and Xanadu entries already in the file.
gaps.would_need: A later pass if a primary document names a machine that is not already in another topic file.
